drills.q: Here is a withdraw() with an external call before the balance deduction. Fix it two ways and rank them.
drills.a: Reentrancy. Fix A: checks-effects-interactions - zero balance BEFORE call, re-entry fails its own check. Fix B: OpenZeppelin nonReentrant mutex. A is primary (covers cross-function variants a per-fn mutex misses); B layered on critical paths.

drills.q: Give an ERC-721 cross-contract reentrancy scenario.
drills.a: _safeMint calls onERC721Received - attacker code runs mid-flow. If minting logic updates accounting AFTER the transfer, attacker reenters via the hook at the inconsistent moment. Defense: finalize all state before ANY token movement; treat every token transfer as potential code execution.

drills.q: What is read-only reentrancy? Name the incident class.
drills.a: View functions report inconsistent state during callbacks: attacker triggers pool X's update, and inside X's callback calls victim V which reads X's view (get_virtual_price) against stale values. Curve pools 2021-23 patched by locking views themselves. Views consumed by other protocols are attack surface.

drills.q: End-to-end: manipulate an AMM spot oracle, then defend it. Include the TWAP caveat.
drills.a: Attack: flash-borrow token B, swap into target pool (constant product: price moves quadratically), protocol lends against inflated collateral, unwind, repay, keep profit - cost = two swaps' fees. Defend: never settle vs own-pool spot; Chainlink deviation ~0.5% + heartbeat staleness; Uniswap V3 TWAP >=30min; caps + breakers. Caveat: ONE manipulated block shifts 30-min TWAP ~+66% - TWAP raises cost, doesn't eliminate.

Oct 11 2022: build long on MNGO perps, pump thin MNGO spot books ~10x in minutes, inflated mark price = huge unrealized PnL usable as collateral, borrow $110M USDC, walk away. Perpetrator convicted April 2024. Preventers: multi-venue median marks, price-band breakers, borrow caps, near-zero collateral factors for illiquid assets.

drills.q: Why did Euler lose $197M despite four audits? What does it teach?
drills.a: March 2023: donation/convertible sub-account interaction - economic composition no reviewer modeled; audits verify specified behavior vs known patterns, not novel compositional economics. Nearly all funds returned via whitehat negotiation - audit failure AND response success simultaneously. Lesson: audits are one input among fuzzing/formal/monitoring/response.

drills.q: Beanstalk $182M: mechanics and the design lesson.
drills.a: April 17 2022: flash-loaned ~$1B, acquired 67% governance weight in ONE block, voted treasury transfer to self, executed, repaid loan - netted $182M in seconds. Lesson: temporally-naive voting is attack surface; add snapshots/multi-block voting, decouple thresholds from transferable tokens.

drills.q: Curve/Vyper July 2023: what actually failed and what's the meta-lesson?
drills.a: Vyper compiler versions 0.2.15/0.3.0 silently disabled @nonreentrant guards - battle-tested pools drained (~$70M) despite clean audit history. Meta: 'dead' bug classes resurrect through toolchain regressions; pin compilers, diff bytecode against source expectations, monitor guard presence.

drills.q: Design the monitoring + response stack for a live lending protocol.
drills.a: Detect: Forta/Tenderly alerts (TVL drop %, utilization spikes, oracle deviation), balance-diff watchers, simulate pending governance proposals. Respond: pause authority matrix (responsive multisig, rehearsed), automated circuit breakers on oracle deviation, standing whitehat channels, Immunefi bounty ($10M-class). Measure time-to-pause as SLO - it bounds loss once prevention fails.

drills.q: Chainlink integration checklist: which checks are mandatory, what remains risky?
drills.a: latestRoundData staleness vs heartbeat (e.g., 1h majors), answeredInRound sanity, price>0, L2 sequencer uptime feed, deviation-from-last bounds. Remains: feed-wide compromise/halt, missing feeds forcing synthetics, L2 latency windows. Mitigate: median across INDEPENDENT providers (correlation!), manual emergency feed behind timelock, treat silence as halt.

drills.q: Are flash loans a vulnerability? Argue precisely.
drills.a: No - amplifier. Atomic (repay or revert), adds unbounded temporary capital: capital-gated attacks (manipulation, governance capture) drop to tx fees. Weaponizes existing flaws: manipulable oracles, instant-finality governance, mispriced collateral. Fix underlying designs; assume free temporary capital in threat models.

drills.q: Compare integer overflow, reentrancy, and oracle manipulation by root-cause layer: which is language-level, code-pattern-level, and architecture-level?
drills.a: Integer overflow: language/compiler-level -- Solidity 0.8's checked-arithmetic default fixed the common case. Reentrancy: code-pattern-level -- the language provides everything needed to write it safely; the fix is developer discipline (CEI) plus tooling (ReentrancyGuard). Oracle manipulation: architecture-level -- no code pattern or compiler default fixes a design decision to trust a manipulable price source; only a different architectural choice (TWAP, decentralized oracle) fixes it.
